text: question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the full title of the main document? answer: FAILURE MECHANISM BASED STRESS TEST QUALIFICATION FOR INTEGRATED CIRCUITS

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the subject of Appendix 1? answer: Appendix 1 of the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document covers the Definition of a Qualification Family. question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the subject of Appendix 2? answer: Appendix 2 of the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document is titled 'Q100 Certification of Design, Construction and Qualification'. question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, which two specific test documents are listed as decommissioned in the attachments? answer: The two specific test documents listed as decommissioned in the attachments are AEC-Q100-003: MACHINE MODEL (MM) ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE (ESD) TEST and AEC-Q100-006: ELECTRO-HERMALLY INDUCED PARASITIC GATE LEAKAGE (GL) TEST.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what does the Revision Summary section describe? answer: The Revision Summary section in the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document describes the changes made in the AEC-Q100 Rev-H document compared to the previous version, AEC-Q100 Rev-G (May 14, 2007). It specifically details modifications to various sections including: Section 1.2.1 - Automotive Reference Documents (added reference to AEC-Q005 Pb-Free Requirements), new Section 1.2.4 - Decommissioned Reference Documents (providing guidance on elimination of AEC-Q100-003 Machine Model ESD and Q100-006 Electrothermally Induced Gate Leakage), Section 1.3.1 - AEC Q100 Qualification (added recommendation about ESD voltage level specification), new Section 1.3.2 - AEC Certification (clarifying that AEC-Q100 'certification' does not exist), Section 1.3.4 - Definition of Part Operating Temperature Grade (added Table 1 and eliminated Grade 4), new Section 1.3.5 - Capability Measure, Cpk (added definition and reference to AEC-Q003), Section 2.2 - Precedence of Requirements (added clarification), and Section 2.3.1 - Definition of Generic Data (moved content to Appendix 1). The summary excludes punctuation and text improvements.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what was added to Section 1.2.1 - Automotive Reference Documents according to the Revision Summary? answer: According to the Revision Summary in the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, a reference to AEC-Q005 Pb-Free Requirements was added to Section 1.2.1 - Automotive Reference Documents.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the purpose of the new Section 1.2.4 as described in the Revision Summary? answer: The purpose of the new Section 1.2.4 - Decommissioned Reference Documents is to provide guidance on the elimination of AEC-Q100-003 Machine Model ESD test and AEC-Q100-006 Electrothermally Induced Gate Leakage test. Specifically, AEC-Q100-003 was removed due to industry test obsolescence, and AEC-Q100-006 was removed due to lack of industry need as a qualification test.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what was added to Section 1.3.1 regarding ESD voltage levels? answer: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 1.3.1 – AEC Q100 Qualification was updated to include a recommendation that the passing ESD voltage level should be specified in the supplier datasheet, along with a footnote noting any pin exceptions.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what does the new Section 1.3.2 clarify about AEC-Q100 'certification'? answer: The new Section 1.3.2 clarifies that AEC-Q100 'certification' does not exist. Instead, suppliers perform qualification testing according to AEC standards.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what change was made to Section 1.3.4 regarding part operating temperature grades? answer: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the change made to Section 1.3.4 regarding part operating temperature grades was the addition of a new Table 1 that defines part operating temperature grades and provides guidance on the use of temperature (such as endpoint and junction) during tests, along with the elimination of the Grade 4 entry.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what new topic and reference were added in Section 1.3.5? answer: In Section 1.3.5, a new topic titled 'Capability Measure, Cpk' was added, which includes a definition of capability measure (Cpk) and a reference to the AEC-Q003 Characterization document.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what sections had clarifications added regarding Precedence of Requirements and the Definition of Generic Data? answer: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 2.2 - Precedence of Requirements had clarifications added to the Purchase Order and Device Specification entries. question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what new section was added under Section 2.3 regarding the acceptance of generic data? answer: Section 2.3.2 - Time Limit for Acceptance of Generic Data was added as a new section under Section 2.3 regarding the acceptance of generic data in the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the purpose of the new Table 1 added in Section 1.3.4? answer: The purpose of the new Table 1 added in Section 1.3.4 is to define part operating temperature grades and provide guidance on the use of temperature (such as endpoint and junction temperatures) during tests. question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what new section was added that defines Capability Measure (Cpk) and which document does it reference? answer: The new section added in the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document is Section 1.3.5 - Capability Measure, Cpk. question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the general subject matter covered by the document? answer: The AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document covers failure mechanism based stress test qualification for packaged integrated circuits. The document contains a set of failure mechanism based stress tests and defines the minimum stress test driven qualification requirements and references test conditions for qualification of integrated circuits (ICs). These tests are designed to stimulate and precipitate semiconductor device and package failures in an accelerated manner compared to use conditions. The purpose is to determine that a device is capable of passing the specified stress tests and thus can be expected to give a certain level of quality/reliability in the application.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what three aspects should each qualification project be examined for, according to the SCOPE? answer: According to the SCOPE section of the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, each qualification project should be examined for: 1) Any potential new and unique failure mechanisms, 2) Any situation where these tests/conditions may induce failures that would not be seen in the application, and 3) Any extreme use condition and/or application that could adversely reduce the acceleration.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, how is the term "user" defined in the SCOPE section? answer: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the term 'user' is defined as all customers using a device qualified per this specification.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, which automotive reference documents are listed in Section 1.2.1? answer: Section 1.2.1 of the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document lists the following automotive reference documents: AEC-Q001 Guidelines for Part Average Testing, AEC-Q002 Guidelines for Statistical Yield Analysis, AEC-Q003 Guidelines for Characterizing the Electrical Performance, AEC-Q004 Zero Defects Guideline (DRAFT), AEC-Q005 Pb-Free Requirements, and SAE J1752/3 Integrated Circuits Radiated Emissions Measurement Procedure.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, which AEC guideline is listed as a DRAFT under the Automotive reference documents? answer: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, under the Automotive reference documents section, AEC-Q004 Zero Defects Guideline is listed as a DRAFT.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what military standard is referenced for test methods and procedures for microelectronics? answer: The military standard referenced for test methods and procedures for microelectronics in the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document is MIL-STD-883.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, which JEDEC standard is listed for Moisture/Reflow Sensitivity Classification for Plastic IC Surface Mount Devices? answer: The JEDEC standard listed for Moisture/Reflow Sensitivity Classification for Plastic IC Surface Mount Devices in the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document is IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what are the JESD89 sub-documents listed, and what do they test for? answer: The AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document lists four JESD89 sub-documents: JESD89, JESD89-1, JESD89-2, and JESD89-3. JESD89 covers measurement and reporting of alpha particle and terrestrial cosmic ray-induced soft errors in semiconductor devices. JESD89-1 is the System Soft Error Rate (SSER) test method. JESD89-2 is the test method for alpha source accelerated soft error rate. JESD89-3 is the test method for beam accelerated soft error rate.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, why were the documents AEC Q100-003 and AEC Q100-006 decommissioned? answer: AEC Q100-003 (ESD Machine Model) was removed from JEDEC due to obsolescence, as HBM and CDM cover virtually all known ESD-related failure mechanisms. AEC Q100-006 (Electrothermally-Induced Gate Leakage) was removed due to the lack of need for it as a qualification test.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what allows a supplier to claim that a part is 'AEC Q100 qualified'? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, successful completion and documentation of the test results from requirements outlined in this document allows the supplier to claim that the part is 'AEC Q100 qualified'. For ESD specifically, it is highly recommended that the passing voltage be specified in the supplier datasheet with a footnote on any pin exceptions, which allows suppliers to state, for example, 'AEC-Q100 qualified to ESD Classification 2'.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is recommended to be specified in the supplier datasheet regarding ESD to allow a specific qualification statement? answer: The AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document recommends that the passing voltage be specified in the supplier datasheet with a footnote on any pin exceptions. This specification enables suppliers to make qualification statements such as 'AEC-Q100 qualified to ESD Classification 2'.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what does the document clarify about 'AEC Certification' and who runs a certification board? answer: The AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document clarifies that there are no 'certifications' for AEC-Q100 qualification and there is no certification board run by AEC to qualify parts. Each supplier performs their own qualification to AEC standards, considers customer requirements, and submits the data to the customer to verify compliance to Q100.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, how is 'Approval for Use in an Application' defined and whose method is beyond the document's scope? answer: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, 'Approval for Use in an Application' is defined as user approval for use of a part in their application. The user's method of approval is beyond the scope of this document.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is specified about the endpoint test temperatures for hot and cold tests relative to the part's operating temperature grade? answer: The AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document specifies that the endpoint test temperatures for hot and cold tests, if required for a particular stress test, must be equivalent to those specified for the particular operating temperature grade. Additionally, if accounting for junction heating during powered tests, the hot test endpoint temperature can be greater than the specified grade temperature. For Test Group B Accelerated Lifetime Simulation Tests including High Temperature Operating Life (HTOL), Early Life Failure Rate (ELFR), and NVM Endurance, Data Retention, and Operational Life (EDR), the junction temperature of the device during stressing should be equal to or greater than the hot temperature for that grade.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, for Test Group B accelerated lifetime tests, what condition must the junction temperature meet relative to the hot temperature for the grade? answer: For Test Group B accelerated lifetime tests, which include High Temperature Operating Life (HTOL), Early Life Failure Rate (ELFR), and NVM Endurance, Data Retention, and Operational Life (EDR), the junction temperature of the device during stressing must be equal to or greater than the hot temperature specified for that grade.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the objective of the specification as stated in section 2.1? answer: The objective of this specification is to establish a standard that defines operating temperature grades for integrated circuits based on a minimum set of qualification requirements.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, which document is referenced to understand how the Cpk measure will be used in this standard? answer: The document referenced to understand how the Cpk measure will be used in the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document is AEC-Q003 Characterization.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, which document contains elements needed to implement a zero defects program? answer: The elements needed to implement a zero defects program can be found in the AEC-Q004 Zero Defects Guideline document.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the order of precedence for requirements in the event of a conflict with other documents, starting with the highest? answer: The order of precedence for requirements in the event of a conflict with other documents, starting with the highest, is: 1) The purchase order (or master purchase agreement terms and conditions), 2) The (mutually agreed) individual device specification, 3) This document (AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document), 4) The reference documents in Section 1.2 of this document, and 5) The supplier's data sheet. For a device to be considered qualified per this specification, the purchase order and/or individual device specification cannot waive or detract from the requirements of this document.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what condition regarding purchase orders or device specifications must be met for a device to be considered a qualified part per this specification? answer: For a device to be considered a qualified part per the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document specification, the purchase order and/or the individual device specification cannot waive or detract from the requirements of this document. This means that any purchase order terms or device specifications must not override, reduce, or eliminate any of the requirements established in the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document specification.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the document's stance on the use of generic data to simplify the qualification process? answer: The AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document strongly encourages the use of generic data to simplify the qualification process. Generic data can be submitted to the user as soon as it becomes available to determine the need for any additional testing. To be considered, the generic data must be based on a matrix of specific requirements associated with each characteristic of the device and manufacturing process as shown in Table 3 and Appendix 1. If the generic data contains any failures, the data is not usable as generic data unless the supplier has documented and implemented corrective action or containment for the failure condition that is acceptable to the user. There are no time limits for the acceptability of generic data, but the data must come from the specific part or a part in the same qualification family as defined in Appendix 1. However, some process changes (e.g., die shrink) will affect the use of generic data such that data obtained before these types of changes will not be acceptable for use as generic data.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, under what condition is generic data containing failures still usable? answer: Generic data containing failures is still usable if the supplier has documented and implemented corrective action or containment for the failure condition that is acceptable to the user.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, where are the criteria defined for grouping components into a qualification family for generic data acceptance? answer: The criteria for grouping components into a qualification family for generic data acceptance are defined in Appendix 1 of the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document. Appendix 1 specifies the criteria by which components are grouped into a qualification family for the purpose of considering the data from all family members to be equal and generically acceptable for the qualification of the device in question.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what does Table 3 define, and for what two purposes is its matrix used? answer: Table 3 defines a set of qualification tests that must be considered for any changes proposed for the component. The Table 3 matrix is used for two purposes: 1) for new processes, and 2) for requalification associated with a process change. The table serves as a superset of tests that the supplier and user should use as a baseline for discussion of tests required for the qualification in question.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, whose responsibility is it to present rationale for omitting recommended tests from Table 3? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, it is the supplier's responsibility to present rationale for why any of the recommended tests from Table 3 need not be performed. Table 3 defines a set of qualification tests that must be considered for any changes proposed for the component, and when determining which tests are required for qualification, the supplier must provide justification for omitting any of the recommended tests.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what are the time limits for the acceptability of generic data? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, there are no time limits for the acceptability of generic data. The document states that generic data must come from the specific part or a part in the same qualification family as defined in Appendix 1. Potential sources of data include customer specific data (with customer name withheld), process change qualification, and periodic reliability monitor data. However, it is noted that some process changes, such as die shrink, will affect the use of generic data such that data obtained before these types of changes will not be acceptable for use as generic data.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, from what sources must reliability data used as generic data come? answer: Reliability data used as generic data must come from the specific part or a part in the same qualification family, as defined in Appendix 1. Potential sources of such data could include customer specific data (with customer name withheld), process change qualification data, and periodic reliability monitor data.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the requirement for test sample composition when multiple lot testing is required due to a lack of generic data? answer: When multiple lot testing is required due to a lack of generic data, test samples must be composed of approximately equal numbers from non-consecutive wafer lots, assembled in non-consecutive molding lots. This means they must be separated in the fabrication or assembly process line by at least one non-qualification lot.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what are the listed sources of data that could be included? answer: The listed sources of data that could be included are customer specific data (with customer name withheld), process change qualification data, and periodic reliability monitor data.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the impact of certain process changes, like a die shrink, on the use of generic data? answer: Certain process changes, such as a die shrink, affect the use of generic data such that data obtained before these types of changes will not be acceptable for use as generic data. This means that when a process change like die shrink occurs, previously collected generic data becomes invalid and cannot be used for qualification purposes.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what are the lot requirements for test samples when multiple lot testing is required due to a lack of generic data? answer: When multiple lot testing is required due to a lack of generic data, test samples as indicated in Table 2 must be composed of approximately equal numbers from non-consecutive wafer lots, assembled in non-consecutive molding lots. This means they must be separated in the fab or assembly process line by at least one non-qualification lot. Any deviation from these requirements requires technical explanation from the supplier.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is required regarding the separation of wafer lots and molding lots for test samples? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, when multiple lot testing is required due to a lack of generic data, test samples must be composed of approximately equal numbers from non-consecutive wafer lots, assembled in non-consecutive molding lots. This means they must be separated in the fab or assembly process line by at least one non-qualification lot. Any deviation from this requirement requires technical explanation from the supplier.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what are the production requirements for qualification devices regarding tooling and processes? answer: All qualification devices shall be produced on tooling and processes at the manufacturing site that will be used to support part deliveries at production volumes. Other electrical test sites may be used for electrical measurements after their electrical quality is validated.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, under what conditions may devices used for nondestructive qualification tests be reused? answer: Devices that have been used for nondestructive qualification tests may be used to populate other qualification tests.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is stipulated about the use of devices that have undergone destructive qualification tests? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, devices that have been used for destructive qualification tests may not be used any further except for engineering analysis. This means that such devices cannot be reused for additional qualification testing or other purposes, with the sole exception being their use for engineering analysis.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what must sample sizes for qualification testing and generic data submission be consistent with? answer: Sample sizes used for qualification testing and/or generic data submission must be consistent with the specified minimum sample sizes and acceptance criteria in Table 2.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what must a supplier do if they elect to use generic data for qualification? answer: If a supplier elects to use generic data for qualification, they must record and make available the specific test conditions and results to the user, preferably in the format shown in Appendix 4. Existing applicable generic data should first be used to satisfy the requirements for each test requirement in Table 2 and those of Section 2.3. Device-specific qualification testing should be performed if the generic data does not satisfy these requirements. Additionally, the supplier must justify the use of generic data and have it approved by the user, and review other devices in the same generic family to ensure there are no common failure mechanisms in that family. Note that some process changes (such as die shrink) will affect the use of generic data, making data obtained before these types of changes unacceptable for use as generic data.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is specified regarding end-point test temperatures for pre- and post-stress tests? answer: End-point test temperatures (room, hot and/or cold) are specified in the 'Additional Requirements' column of Table 2 for each test.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, how are test failures after stressing defined? answer: Test failures after stressing are defined as devices that do not meet the individual device specification, criteria specific to the test, or the supplier's data sheet, following the order of significance defined in Section 2.2. Additionally, any device showing external physical damage attributable to the environmental test is considered a failed device. If a failure is due to mishandling during stressing or testing (such as EOS or ESD) or some other cause unrelated to component reliability, the failure is discounted but must still be reported as part of the data submission.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what must a supplier have available for the qualification of a new device, as outlined in Section 3.1? answer: For the qualification of a new device, the supplier must have available the following: 1) Certificate of Design, Construction and Qualification (see Appendix 2), 2) Stress Test Qualification data (see Table 2 & Appendix 4), and 3) Data indicating the level of fault grading of the software used for qualification (when applicable to the device type) per Q100-007 that will be made available to the customer upon request. Additionally, the supplier must have data available for all stress tests, whether it is stress test results on the device to be qualified or acceptable generic data. A review must also be made of other devices in the same generic family to ensure there are no common failure mechanisms in that family. Justification for the use of generic data, whenever it is used, must be demonstrated by the supplier and approved by the user.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, when is requalification of a device required? answer: Requalification of a device is required when the supplier makes a change to the product and/or process that impacts (or could potentially impact) the form, fit, function, quality and/or reliability of the device. Table 3 provides guidelines for such changes requiring requalification.
question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what will the supplier do regarding Process Change Notification? answer: The supplier will meet the user requirements for product/process changes.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what must be done with a failure caused by mishandling during stressing or testing? answer: If the cause of failure is due to mishandling during stressing or testing such as EOS or ESD, or some other cause unrelated to the component reliability, the failure shall be discounted but reported as part of the data submission.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what documents and data must a supplier have available for device qualification? answer: For device qualification according to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, a supplier must have available the following documents and data: 1) Certificate of Design, Construction and Qualification (as specified in Appendix 2), 2) Stress Test Qualification data (as specified in Table 2 and Appendix 4), and 3) Data indicating the level of fault grading of the software used for qualification (when applicable to the device type) per Q100-007, which will be made available to the customer upon request.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, under what condition is requalification of a device required? answer: Requalification of a device is required when the supplier makes a change to the product and/or process that impacts (or could potentially impact) the form, fit, function, quality and/or reliability of the device. As a minimum, any change to the product, as defined in Appendix 1, requires performing the applicable tests listed in Table 2, using Table 3 to determine the requalification test plan. Table 3 should be used as a guide for determining which tests are applicable to the qualification of a particular part change or whether equivalent generic data can be submitted for that test(s).

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the supplier's obligation regarding Process Change Notification? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the supplier's obligation regarding Process Change Notification is that the supplier will meet the user requirements for product/process changes. This requirement is specified in section 3.2.1 of the document, which states that when changes are made to a product and/or process that impact or could potentially impact the form, fit, function, quality, and/or reliability of the device, the supplier must comply with user requirements for those changes as part of the requalification process.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the minimum requirement for requalification when a product change occurs as defined in Appendix 1? answer: As a minimum, any change to the product as defined in Appendix 1 requires performing the applicable tests listed in Table 2, using Table 3 to determine the requalification test plan. Table 3 should be used as a guide for determining which tests are applicable to the qualification of a particular part change or whether equivalent generic data can be submitted for those tests.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, how is Table 3 used in the requalification process? answer: Table 3 is used as a guide in the requalification process to determine which tests are applicable for qualifying a particular part change or whether equivalent generic data can be submitted for those tests. When a supplier makes changes to a product that impact form, fit, function, quality, and/or reliability, requalification is required. As a minimum, any change to the product requires performing applicable tests listed in Table 2, and Table 3 is used to determine the requalification test plan. Specifically, Table 3 provides guidelines for determining which tests apply to the qualification of a particular part change and whether equivalent generic data can be submitted for that test or tests.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what must be done with requalification failures before a part can be considered AEC Q100 qualified again? answer: All requalification failures must be analyzed for root cause. Only when corrective and preventative actions are in place, the part may then be considered AEC Q100 qualified again.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is required for user approval of a process change that may affect a device's performance in an application? answer: Individual user authorization of a process change will be required for that user's particular application(s) when a change may affect a device's performance in an application, even if it does not affect the device's operating temperature grade. This method of authorization is outside the scope of the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, which document specifies added requirements for the qualification of a Pb-Free Device? answer: The added requirements needed to address the special quality and reliability issues for qualification of a Pb-Free Device are specified in AEC-Q005 Pb-Free Requirements. This document covers the requirements that arise when Lead (Pb)-Free processing is utilized, including considerations for termination plating, board attach materials, higher processing temperatures, moisture sensitivity levels, and potential need for more robust mold compounds.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what materials used in Pb-Free processing are mentioned as requiring higher board attach temperatures? answer: The materials used in Pb-Free processing that require higher board attach temperatures are termination plating and board attach (solder). These new materials typically need elevated temperatures to achieve acceptable solder joint quality and reliability.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, why might new, more robust mold compounds be required for Pb-Free devices? answer: New, more robust mold compounds may be required for Pb-Free devices because Pb-Free processing uses materials that require higher board attach temperatures to achieve acceptable solder joint quality and reliability. These higher temperatures can adversely affect the moisture sensitivity level of plastic packaged semiconductors, necessitating the use of more robust mold compounds to maintain adequate performance and reliability under these conditions.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what should a supplier do if an encapsulation material change is needed for Pb-Free processing robustness? answer: If an encapsulation material change is required to provide adequate robustness for Pb-Free processing of the device, the supplier should refer to the process change qualification requirements in the AEC-Q100 specification. This includes performing preconditioning at the Pb-free reflow classification temperatures described in IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 Moisture/Reflow Sensitivity Classification for Non-Hermetic Solid State Surface Mount Devices before environmental stress tests.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is indicated in the 'Note' column of Table 2 regarding qualification tests? answer: The 'Note' column of Table 2 indicates which qualification tests are applicable for particular device types. Not all tests apply to all devices, as certain tests apply only to specific device types such as ceramic packaged devices, devices with NVM (non-volatile memory), and others. The 'Note' column serves to specify the applicable tests for each particular device type being qualified.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the purpose of the 'Additional Requirements' column in Table 2? answer: The 'Additional Requirements' column in Table 2 serves to highlight test requirements that supersede those described in the referenced test method. It identifies specific qualification test requirements that take precedence over the standard test methods referenced elsewhere in the document.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, which three tests must be performed as Device Specific Tests, for which generic data is not allowed? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the three tests that must be performed as Device Specific Tests, for which generic data is not allowed, are: 1) Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) - All product, 2) Latch-up (LU) - All product, and 3) Electrical Distribution - The supplier must demonstrate, over the operating temperature grade, voltage, and frequency, that the device is capable of meeting the parametric limits of the device specification. These tests must be performed on the specific device to be qualified for all hermetic and plastic packaged devices, and generic data is not allowed for these tests.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what are the requirements for the Electrical Distribution test data regarding lots and statistical validity? answer: For the Electrical Distribution test, the data must be taken from at least three lots, or one matrixed (or skewed) process lot, and must represent enough samples to be statistically valid, as referenced in Q100-009.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what tests must be performed on the specific device to be qualified for all hermetic and plastic packaged devices? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the following tests must be performed on the specific device to be qualified for all hermetic and plastic packaged devices: Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) for all products, Latch-up (LU) for all products, and Electrical Distribution testing. For Electrical Distribution, the supplier must demonstrate over the operating temperature grade, voltage, and frequency that the device is capable of meeting the parametric limits of the device specification. This data must be taken from at least three lots, or one matrixed (or skewed) process lot, and must represent enough samples to be statistically valid. Generic data is not allowed for these tests, though device-specific data that already exists is acceptable. Additionally, wearout reliability tests must be available to the user whenever a new technology or material relevant to appropriate wearout failure mechanisms is to be qualified, including Electromigration, Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (or Gate Oxide Integrity Test) for all MOS technologies, Hot Carrier Injection for all MOS technologies below 1 micron, Negative Bias Temperature Instability, and Stress Migration.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is stated about the use of generic data for the required tests on specific devices? answer: The AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document explicitly states that generic data is not allowed for the required tests that must be performed on specific devices to be qualified. These mandatory tests include Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) for all products, Latch-up (LU) for all products, and Electrical Distribution testing. For these specific qualification tests, only device-specific data is acceptable, though existing device-specific data can be used if it already exists. The document does provide guidelines in Appendix 1 for using generic data in appropriate circumstances to streamline the qualification process, but this does not apply to the core required tests mentioned above. For other tests not specifically listed as mandatory, users may require additional tests in place of generic data based on their experience with particular suppliers.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, for which products is the Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) test required? answer: The Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) test is required for all products according to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document. The document explicitly states that ESD testing applies to 'All product' without any exceptions or qualifications based on package type or other characteristics.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what are the requirements for the Electrical Distribution test data regarding production lots and statistical validity? answer: For the Electrical Distribution test, the supplier must demonstrate that the device is capable of meeting the parametric limits of the device specification over the operating temperature grade, voltage, and frequency. The data must be taken from at least three production lots, or one matrixed (or skewed) process lot. Additionally, the data must represent enough samples to be statistically valid, as referenced in Q100-009. It is strongly recommended that the final test limits be established using AEC-Q001 Guidelines For Part Average Testing.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what guideline is strongly recommended for establishing final test limits for Electrical Distribution? answer: The AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document strongly recommends that final test limits for Electrical Distribution be established using AEC-Q001 Guidelines For Part Average Testing.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, under what condition may a user require other tests in lieu of generic data? answer: A user may require other tests in lieu of generic data based on their experience with a particular supplier.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, when must testing for the listed wearout reliability failure mechanisms be available to the user? answer: Testing for the listed wearout reliability failure mechanisms must be available to the user whenever a new technology or material relevant to the appropriate wearout failure mechanism is to be qualified. The data, test method, calculations, and internal criteria should be available to the user upon request, though they need not be demonstrated or performed on the qualification of every new device.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, which wearout reliability test is specified for all MOS technologies below 1 micron? answer: Hot Carrier Injection is the wearout reliability test specified for all MOS technologies below 1 micron in the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what does the note 'H' in the legend for Table 2 indicate about a test requirement? answer: The note 'H' in the legend for Table 2 indicates that a test requirement is required for hermetic packaged devices only.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the meaning of the note 'D' in the legend for Table 2 regarding test types? answer: The note 'D' in the legend for Table 2 indicates that the test is a destructive test, meaning that devices subjected to this test cannot be reused for qualification or production purposes.
question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, for which type of devices is the note 'L' in Table 3 applicable? answer: Note 'L' in Table 3 is applicable for Pb-free devices only.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the purpose of Appendix 1 as described in the text? answer: Appendix 1 provides guidelines for the use of generic data to accelerate and streamline the qualification process for suppliers and customers. It defines what constitutes a product qualification family, establishing that devices must share the same major product, process, and materials elements to be categorized together. This appendix serves as a guideline for suppliers and customers to reach mutual agreement on how to utilize generic data when appropriate.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what must all devices share to be categorized in a product qualification family? answer: All devices must share the same major product, process and materials elements. Specifically, they must share the same critical product functional details, critical process steps, and critical materials as defined in the document's sections A1.1, A1.2, and A1.3 respectively.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, to what limits is all electrical testing performed before and after qualification stresses? answer: All electrical testing before and after qualification stresses are performed to the limits of the individual device specification in temperature and limit value.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what does a letter or '●' indicate in Table 3 regarding stress tests for process changes? answer: In Table 3 of the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, a letter or '●' indicates that performance of that particular stress test should be considered for the appropriate process change. The note specifies that if a test is considered but not performed, the reason for not performing it must be documented in the qualification plan or results. The letters (A through T) correspond to specific types of process changes, such as 'A' for peripheral routing only, 'B' for symbol rework with new cure time and temperature, 'C' if bonding to leadfinger, and so on through the various process change categories listed in the table.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what do the letters L, M, N, Q, and T in the initial list represent? answer: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the letters L, M, N, Q, and T in the initial list represent specific device categories or requirements. L represents devices that are for Pb-free devices only. M represents devices that require PTC (Positive Temperature Coefficient). N represents passivation and gate oxide requirements. Q represents wire diameter decrease specifications. T represents devices that are for Solder Ball SMD only.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the purpose of the guideline provided in Appendix 1 for defining a Product Qualification Family? answer: The purpose of the guideline provided in Appendix 1 for defining a Product Qualification Family is to accelerate and streamline the qualification process for suppliers and customers. It enables suppliers and customers to reach mutual agreement on how to utilize generic data when it is appropriate. This guideline allows devices that share the same major product, process, and materials elements to be categorized in a product qualification family, where the qualification of one family member successfully completing qualification qualifies all products in the same family by association, with the exception of device-specific requirements.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what must all devices share to be categorized in the same product qualification family? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, for devices to be categorized in the same product qualification family, they all must share the same major product, process and materials elements. The critical product functional details defined in Section A1.1 and critical process steps and materials defined in Sections A1.2 and A1.3 do not need to be matched exactly, but shall cover worst cases in application of the family generic data through technical justification. All products in the same product qualification family are qualified by association when one family member successfully completes qualification, with the exception of the device specific requirements of Section 4.2.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, how are products in the same family qualified when one member completes qualification, and what is the exception? answer: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, all products in the same product qualification family are qualified by association when one family member successfully completes qualification. The exception to this is the device specific requirements of Section 4.2, which are not covered by the family qualification process and must be addressed separately for each device.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what should be done for broad changes involving multiple attributes like site, materials, or processes? answer: For broad changes that involve multiple attributes such as site, materials, or processes, the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document states that one should refer to Section A1.5 of Appendix 1 and Section 2.3 of Q100. These sections allow for the selection of worst-case test vehicles to cover all the possible permutations of the changes.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what are the key product attributes listed under Section A1.1 for defining a product qualification family? answer: The key product attributes listed under Section A1.1 for defining a product qualification family are: Product functionality (e.g., Op-Amp, regulator, microprocessor, Logic - HC/TTL), Operating supply voltage range(s), Specified operating temperature range, Specified operating frequency range, Design library cells for the fab technology, Memory IP (e.g., cell structure, building block), Digital design library cells (e.g., circuit blocks, IO modules, ESD cells) and/or analog design library cells (e.g., active circuit elements, passive circuit elements) at data sheet voltage level(s) and at data sheet or better temperature range, and power dissipation, Speed/performance of the library cells, Memory type(s) and sizes, Design rules for active circuits under pads, and Other functional characteristics as defined by supplier.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what specific requirement is stated for parts operating at different power supply voltages? answer: For parts specified to operate at different power supplies (e.g., 5.0 V and 3.3 V), product qualification family data should be presented for both supply ranges.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what data presentation is required for parts specified to operate at different temperature ranges? answer: For parts specified to operate at different temperature ranges, three (3) lots of data from the product qualification family at the temperature of the device in the data sheet need to be presented with Table 2 E1 TEST data. Stress classification at the temperature specified in Q100 Table 2 groups A, B, E, and G must be equal to or higher than the device being qualified.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is the requirement regarding memory types and sizes for qualification within a family? answer: According to the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, for memory types and sizes within a product qualification family, all memory types must be demonstrated to be qualified over three (3) lots using the largest memory size to be qualified for devices in the family. If the part to be qualified has a larger memory size than the one already qualified, the supplier must perform at least one lot of testing on the larger memory configuration. This requirement is part of the product qualification family guidelines where memory type(s) and sizes are listed as one of the product functionality characteristics that must be considered.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what must be considered separately regarding fab process technology according to Section A1.2? answer: According to Section A1.2, each process technology (e.g., CMOS, NMOS, Bipolar) must be considered and qualified separately. No matter how similar, processes from one fundamental fab technology cannot be used for another. For BiCMOS devices, data must be taken from the appropriate technology based on the circuit under consideration.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is required for BiCMOS devices in terms of data collection for qualification? answer: For BiCMOS devices, data must be taken from the appropriate technology based on the circuit under consideration. This means that qualification data collection must be specific to the particular technology and circuit being evaluated, rather than using generic data from different technologies.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, when is a 'worst case' family requalification required according to the fab process section? answer: According to the fab process section of the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, a 'worst case' family requalification with the appropriate tests is required when the process or a material is changed. question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what does the fab process attribute 'Circuit element feature size' include as examples? answer: The fab process attribute 'Circuit element feature size' includes examples such as layout design rules, die shrinks, contacts, gates, and isolations.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what must a supplier justify regarding the number of masks in the fab process? answer: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, a supplier must show justification for waiving the requirement related to the number of masks in the fab process. The number of masks is listed as one of the important attributes defining a fab process, and if a supplier wishes to waive this requirement when categorizing devices in a product qualification family, they must provide technical justification for doing so.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, why cannot processes from one fundamental fab technology be used for another, even if they are similar? answer: Processes from one fundamental fab technology cannot be used for another because each fab technology has specific attributes that define its unique characteristics. The important attributes defining a fab process include: wafer fab technology (e.g., CMOS, NMOS, Bipolar), circuit element feature size (e.g., layout design rules, die shrinks, contacts, gates, isolations), substrate characteristics (e.g., orientation, doping, epi, wafer size), number of masks, lithographic process (e.g., contact vs. projection, E-beam vs. X-ray, photoresist polarity), doping process (e.g., diffusion vs. ion implantation), gate structure, material and process (e.g., polysilicon, metal, salicide, wet vs. dry etch), polysilicon material, thickness range and number of levels, oxidation process and thickness range (e.g., gate and field oxides), interlayer dielectric material and thickness range, metallization material, thickness range and number of levels, passivation process (e.g., passivation oxide opening), material and thickness range, and die backside preparation process and metallization. For BiCMOS devices specifically, data must be taken from the appropriate technology based on the circuit under consideration. Worst case family requalification with appropriate tests is required when the process or a material is changed, as different technologies have fundamentally different process elements and material characteristics that affect device performance and reliability.

question: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, what is required when a process or material is changed for wafer fab technology, and where are the guidelines found? answer: When a process or material is changed for wafer fab technology, worst case family requalification with the appropriate tests is required.
